blocks.text: False reasoning arises from what is primarily false. For every syllogism consists of two or more propositions, if then it consists of two, it is necessary that one or both of these should be false, for there would not be a false syllogism from true propositions. But if of more than two, as if C (is proved) through A B, and these through D E F G, some one of the above is false, and on this account the reasoning also, since A and B are concluded through them. Hence through some one of them the conclusion and the false occur.
